The stained glass window behind the pulpit went from a bright red cross to a smear of pink. I heard Pastor Whitfield say something about the blood of the lamb but his voice sounded like it was coming from under water.

I was diagnosed with Chronic Trapezius Tension at 33. I'm 45 now. Turns out I never had a trapezius problem at all. My muscles were tight because something else was making them tight — and no one in twelve years of physical therapy, massage, or ergonomic consultation ever screened me for what was actually firing them.
For twelve years, I "managed" a condition I didn't actually have.

Twelve years of weekly deep-tissue massage. Same therapist. Rachel. She has known the exact knot in my right trap by name for over a decade. She calls it "the boulder." She has spent probably 500 hours of her life

My granddaughter asked me why I wasn't eating my own pie.

She's 7. So she just said it, the way 7-year-olds do. Standing there at the table, holding a paper plate with a slice of my sweet potato pie on it, looking up at me like she'd caught me doing something wrong.

"Grandma. How come you're not having any?"

And I just stood there.

My granddaughter announced her engagement on a Sunday and I told her yes before she finished asking.

She wanted me to make the cake.

I said yes and I smiled and I hugged her and I told her Grandma wouldn't miss it for the world.

Then I drove home and sat in my car in the driveway for 40 minutes crying so hard my glasses fogged up and I had to take them off and set them on the dashboard.

Because I haven't touched a piping bag in two and a half years.

My husband couldn't get up off the toilet on a Tuesday in March and I had to call our son to drive over and break the door down.

He sat on that floor for 40 minutes before he finally yelled for me.

35 years married and I'd never heard him cry like that.
